title: The Tryouts of the quarry
premise: Paloma Yarrow has spent seventeen years being the quiet baker's daughter in the quarry town of Kilnrock, folding her grief and longing into loaves nobody questions. When she opens her late grandmother's recipe box, she finds cards that aren't recipes at all but coded instructions—addresses, names, dates—belonging to a secret network of 'tryouts' who tested the town's powerful men and delivered justice the law never would. Following the cards, Paloma discovers her grandmother was its founder and that the network's last unfinished trial targets the quarry owner whose negligence killed her father. As the town closes in and her found family of fellow tryouts risks exposure, Paloma must choose between the invisible life she planned and the dangerous inheritance of memory and justice, ending with her serving the truth like bread—openly, to everyone—at a cost she never expected but can finally carry.
about_author: Beatrix Crane is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering mill towns and the silences they keep. She writes young adult fiction about kids who inherit secrets too heavy for their pockets.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Three weeks before graduation, Paloma works the bakery's dawn shift, kneading her dread into sourdough and counting days like a sentence. Her mother's grief and the town's pity keep her invisible. Emotional beat: suffocating stasis, the ache of a life on hold.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Sorting her grandmother's things, Paloma finds cards in the old tin: 'For Justice, preheat the town to a slow boil.' The cards reference people—some dead, some disgraced, some still powerful. Emotional beat: vertigo, the floor of her ordinary life giving way.

chapters.title: First Card
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She follows one card to a shuttered grange hall and meets Dez, a mechanic's kid, and Auntie Vess, her grandmother's oldest friend. They reveal the Tryouts: a generations-old circle that tested the guilty when Kilnrock's law protected them. Emotional beat: terrified belonging.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Ate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Paloma and Dez. The final unfinished card names Hollis Vane, quarry owner, whose collapsed wall killed six men—including Paloma's father—five years ago. The case died with her grandmother. Emotional beat: rage surfacing through grief like a bruise.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Practicing the Tryouts' methods—observation, testimony, memory—Paloma realizes her bread-baking is itself a tool: people confess to the girl with flour on her hands. Her best friend Theo grows suspicious of her absences. Emotional beat: first taste of her own power, and its loneliness.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez tracks a retired quarry foreman who saw the unsafe wall and stayed silent for a paycheck. Convincing him means risking his family's only income. Emotional beat: the weight of mercy versus justice, and what silence costs.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vane's son, Paloma's classmate Eli, starts asking questions of his own—about his father, about her. Meanwhile Vane announces he'll demolish the quarry memorial to build a resort. The Tryouts must move before the evidence is literally bulldozed. Emotional beat: ticking clock, loyalty pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Kneaded Under
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A raid on the grange hall scatters the Tryouts; Auntie Vess is detained, and Paloma's name surfaces. Theo discovers her secret and, hurt by the lies, walks away. Emotional beat: betrayal on all sides, the inheritance turning to a burden.

chapters.title: The Tryout of Hollis Vane
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, climax. Instead of the old secret ritual, Paloma bakes the truth into a hundred loaves—each wrapped in testimony—and delivers them across Kilnrock on graduation morning. The town reads while Vane rages; the foreman testifies; Eli stands with his father's victims. Emotional beat: justice done in daylight, terrifying and liberating.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, resolution. Vane faces a reopened investigation; Auntie Vess is released; Theo returns with flour-dusted hands, asking to learn. Paloma takes her grandmother's place—not to hide, but to hand the recipe box, one day, to whoever needs it next. Emotional beat: found family, chosen identity, grief finally given somewhere to go.
